title: Palindrome Partitioning
keyIdea: Backtracking on the first piece: for every end i from start, if s[start..i] is a palindrome, take it and partition the rest from i + 1, then remove it. start == n → save. Optionally precompute pal[i][j] so each check is O(1).

approaches.name: Precomputed palindrome table
approaches.idea: Fill pal[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] && (j − i < 2 || pal[i + 1][j − 1]) bottom-up, then backtrack with O(1) lookups.
approaches.why: Same number of partitions; each palindrome check drops from O(n) to O(1).

approaches.name: Backtracking + two-pointer check
approaches.idea: for i from start: sub = s[start..i]; if isPalindrome(sub): push, backtrack(i + 1), pop.
approaches.why: Up to 2ⁿ⁻¹ ways to cut the string, each built and checked in O(n).

quiz.q: What does each loop step in backtrack decide?
options: Where the current first piece ends

quiz.q: Why only recurse when the piece is a palindrome?
options: A non-palindrome piece can never be part of a valid answer, so that branch is cut

quiz.q: In the table version, why fill rows from the bottom (i = n − 1 down)?
options: pal[i][j] needs pal[i + 1][j − 1], which is in the row below
